pr_body:
### What does it do?

use existing transaction to batchInsert

potential fix for #21352 and #21395 if someone can please confirm it fixes those

### Why is it needed?

query was not using the correct knex object

### How to test it?

Provide information about the environment and the path to verify the behaviour.

### Related issue(s)/PR(s)

DX-1630

fixes #21352 

fixes #21395

Fixes the (or another) problem at a different level: https://github.com/strapi/strapi/pull/21412 will investigate shortly; my feeling is we would like both that fix and this fix

## Bug report

### Required System information

<!-- Please ensure you are using the Node LTS version (v18 or v20) -->
<!-- Strapi v3 is no longer supported, please update to Strapi v4 -->
<!-- If you are reporting a frontend bug please provide error logs after setting STRAPI_ENFORCE_SOURCEMAPS=true in your .env -->
<!-- This environment variable makes frontend errors easier to read and trace -->

- Node.js version: v18.20.4
- NPM version: 10.7.0
- Strapi version: 5.0.0
- Database: PostgreSQL
- Operating system: Windows 10 21H2 (LTSC)
- Is your project Javascript or Typescript: Typescript

<!-- Did you know you can run `yarn strapi report` or `npm run strapi report` to get this information easier? -->

### Describe the bug

When I upgrade to Strapi 5.0.0 and run Strapi for the first time, I get a migration error:

```
[2024-09-20 00:00:01.604] error: Migration core::5.0.0-discard-drafts (up) failed: Original error: con.batchInsert is not a function
MigrationError: Migration core::5.0.0-discard-drafts (up) failed: Original error: con.batchInsert is not a function
    at C:\Users\jackb\Workspace\content-manager\node_modules\umzug\lib\umzug.js:169:27
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:95:5)
    at async Umzug.runCommand (C:\Users\jackb\Workspace\content-manager\node_modules\umzug\lib\umzug.js:125:20)
    at async Object.up (C:\Users\jackb\Workspace\content-manager\node_modules\@strapi\database\dist\index.js:6531:7)
    at async Object.up (C:\Users\jackb\Workspace\content-manager\node_modules\@strapi\database\dist\index.js:6555:11)
    at async Object.sync (C:\Users\jackb\Workspace\content-manager\node_modules\@strapi\database\dist\index.js:2246:9)
    at async Strapi.bootstrap (C:\Users\jackb\Workspace\content-manager\node_modules\@strapi\core\dist\Strapi.js:351:5)
    at async Strapi.load (C:\Users\jackb\Workspace\content-manager\node_modules\@strapi\core\dist\Strapi.js:315:5)
    at async Strapi.start (C:\Users\jackb\Workspace\content-manager\node_modules\@strapi\core\dist\Strapi.js:207:9)
[2024-09-20 00:00:01.606] info: Shutting down Strapi
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Upgrade from Strapi 4.25.10.
2. Make a testing/development copy of the database from 4.25.10 and configure Strapi to use the copy.
3. Start Strapi.
4. After several minutes, the migration fails.

### Expected behavior

The migration should not fail.

### Additional context

This is probably related to https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/21352.
